title: Polygraphia row reuse raises one-edit matches but leaves a large glyph-entropy gap
statement: Using a row for multiple successive plaintext letters sharply increases the one-edit share of adjacent Polygraphia III ciphertext words. In an exploratory follow-up with a one-eighth chance of staying on the current row, the 40- and 48-row settings overlap the public-training sample’s word entropy and adjacent one-edit rate, but their within-word conditional raw-character entropy is 2.276–2.483 bits versus the sample’s 1.536. These settings and controls were chosen after earlier exploratory results and do not constitute a joint fit, a historical reconstruction or an unknown-key recovery.
check: Independently fix row counts, row-selection procedure, exact tokenizer, metric definitions, uncertainty and acceptance ranges before using new plaintext and cipher keys. Compare all four statistics jointly, using public evaluation and independent texts only after choices are frozen; add relevant historical selection rules and noise. Develop a trusted declarative evaluator and calibrated unknown-key search with planted positives and matched search budgets, including the cost and recoverability of the row schedule. Do not register a hidden-page claim or exclude a language/cipher cell based on these descriptive pilots.
common_method: Use the first 5,000 certain lowercase ASCII paragraph tokens of ZL public practice-training pages as the fixed layout and baseline. Never join across line ends or uncertain tokens. Calculate plug-in word entropy, raw-character entropy, H(next raw character | previous raw character) within words, and the share of adjacent unequal words at Levenshtein distance one. Take three previously unused plaintext works, Villani, Roman de la Rose and Chaucer, verify pinned hashes and normalize with vs.refcorpus.blocks_of, retaining only symbols present in the 24-letter Hermes table. These three works are distinct but their windows and per-key outputs are not independent texts.
block_experiment: For each of 10, 24 and 120 fixed initial table rows, advance to the next row after every 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 plaintext letters, cyclically. Use three nonoverlapping 5,000-letter windows at offsets 0, 5,000 and 10,000 of each book. The same word layout is used for every sample. For each setting the evaluator knows all rows and the schedule and exactly inverts all 5,000 characters; this is not unknown-key recovery.
random_experiment: After seeing the block experiment, explore independent random decisions to stay on the current row with probabilities 1/8, 1/4 or 1/2, otherwise advance one row cyclically. Use the next, disjoint 5,000-letter window at offset 15,000, three fixed seeds (113, 271, 449), and initially the same 10, 24 and 120 rows. After inspecting those outputs, add 40, 48 and 64 rows at probability 1/8 on the same windows and seeds. Thus those values are adaptively selected on this public comparison and cannot serve as independent validation. Knowing the actual random schedule and table exactly recovers the plaintext; the cost and unknown-key recoverability of that schedule are not measured.
source: Hermes P.III CSV at https://github.com/hermesj/R_Voynich_Stats/blob/0ef1439fa9d90aeab42951a51d0d5a0e27db1f8f/R%20code/Historical_ciphers/keys/ciphers_poly_III_in_order.csv, SHA-256 fe3f24a46dbc6b655eab8dbbd75addf84ee4a7dbd387ad802af75d02edfe5b4d. The complete metric and input validation script is embedded below.
limitations: The previous cyclic pilot and this adaptation were motivated by observed public manuscript patterns; choices are not preregistered, and this is not a statistical test or a hidden-page result. The two overlapping metrics do not correct the substantial conditional-glyph gap, and conditional entropy here is in raw characters, not EVA-basic units. Three texts and correlated seeds/window samples cannot support general power or uncertainty claims. The stochastic rule is synthetic, not demonstrated historical practice. A known-key round-trip does not establish unknown-key search power. Several required declarative scorer and multi-metric registration pieces remain unimplemented.
